exceptions.rationale: No portable ethers database entry is guaranteed to exist; success is accepted when the host provides one, while the documented missing-entry result is reported otherwise.
No portable ethers database entry is guaranteed to exist; success is accepted when the host provides one, while the documented missing-entry result is reported otherwise.
The native smoke supplies a zeroed inactive AIO control block and verifies that the wrapper reports the operating system's rejection.
aio_return requires a completed request whose result has not already been collected; the smoke verifies rejection of an inactive control block.
The zero-entry list is a bounded deterministic native rejection and avoids manufacturing an asynchronous request with timing-dependent completion.
The native smoke supplies a zeroed inactive AIO control block and verifies that the wrapper reports the operating system's rejection.
A zeroed analysis options object and missing observer are deliberately invalid; the native smoke verifies the wrapper's deterministic defensive rejection.
A zero-sized output buffer is deliberately invalid; the native smoke verifies the wrapper's deterministic defensive rejection.
A zero message-catalog descriptor is safely detectable and must be rejected before libc can dereference it.
A zero message-catalog descriptor is safely detectable; the wrapper reports EBADF and returns the caller's fallback text.
No portable message catalog is guaranteed to exist; the smoke uses a deliberately absent catalog and verifies the ordinary ENOENT path.
The default bad-transition handler exists specifically to turn an unknown transition into a typed refusal; the native smoke verifies that deterministic policy boundary.
The smoke uses an empty list and verifies its deterministic rejection rather than creating timing-dependent asynchronous I/O.
Changing niceness is host-policy dependent even in a subprocess; success is preferred, while only the documented permission refusals are accepted.
The bounded native smoke wakes pause with SIGALRM; POSIX therefore requires an EINTR failure result.
The smoke uses the invalid resource value -1 so it cannot mutate the process limits; the wrapper rejects it before dispatch.
Changing process priority is host-policy dependent even when lowering priority; success is preferred, while only documented permission refusals are accepted.
The bounded native smoke wakes sigsuspend with SIGALRM; POSIX therefore requires an EINTR failure result.
